The Bad Creek Project is designed to withstand the catastrophic natural phenomena of a probable maximum flood and an earthquake having a ground acceleration of 0.10 gravity. An emergency spillway in the upper reservoir would provide safety against overpumping in case of malfunction of the pumping trip-off devices. Transmission lines are designed to withstand high winds. The probability of flooding the powerhouse is very remote, and in the event of flooding, egress could be negotiated by one access tunnel and the vertical bus shaft.
1.7 FUTURE PLANS
The Applicant does not plan to expand the Bad Creek Project; however, there are other potential pumped storage sites in the general area which are being considered. (See Subsection 8.3, ALTERNATIVE SITES.) Upon issuance of a license, Applicant would be required to file an Emergency-Action Plan with the Commission. This plan would describe actions to be taken in the event of a dam failure.
1.8 COMPLIANCE WITH APPLICABLE LAWS AND REGULATIONS
The Applicant has obtained a Water Quality Certificate pursuant to Section 401 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act Amendments of 1972 (Act) from the State of South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (DHEC). Applicant proposes to treat domestic wastes during construction by use of a portable sewage treatment plant. If the discharge from this plant is made into a stream or into Lake Jocassee, the Applicant would be required to obtain a water quality certificate and discharge permit pursuant to Sections 401 and 402 of the Act. Similar permits would be required during operation for the discharge from any treatment plant used to treat domestic wastes at the powerhouse.
Applicant proposes to adhere to all applicable codes and regulations in the construction, maintenance, and operation of the project. Table 1-1 shows permits or licenses required for the Bad Creek Project and the proposed dates of application for each.
